To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

psychology training programs in a large state in the southeastern United States are not adequately training psychology trainees in the areas of adolescent health, nutrition, and medicine, but do have opportunities to increase training in these areas.
psychology training programs in a large southern state are not providing adequate interdisciplinary training in adolescent health care.

(a) adolescent health issues are included in many psychology training programs in a southeastern state and often involve the discipline of psychiatry; (b) adolescent health issues may be integrated into psychology training programs in ways that enhance psychology's ability as a vital component to adolescent health care teams in academic medical centers; and (c) opportunities for interdisciplinary training of psychology trainees in adolescent health care exist in psychology training in this southeastern state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the social context in which people live and work affects their health.
how to improve the quality of care and services provided to adolescents.
how to improve the quality of life of adolescents and young adults with chronic illnesses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a need for interdisciplinary training in adolescent health issues in psychology programs.
there is a need for more training in adolescent health care in the predoctoral programs in psychology.
the current training of predoctoral psychologists is deficient in terms of the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to work with adolescents in health care settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the training needs of psychology interns in adolescent health care is a significant area of concern for many psychology training programs in the Southeast.
we need to be more aware of the interdisciplinary training needs in our programs.
we have developed a model for interdisciplinary training in adolescent health care that could be replicated across the country.

psychology training programs need more opportunities to collaborate with other disciplines in the health sciences, especially with the medical and nursing professions. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
